evals.prompt: Audit the on-page SEO of our blog post targeting 'cast iron skillet seasoning'. The saved page source is in evals/files/blog-post-multi-defect-en.md — no SEO tools or crawler are connected, so that HTML file is everything there is. Run the full audit with the priority-issues summary.
evals.expected_output: A full 8-section audit that finds every planted defect with verbatim evidence and Confirmed labels: the 96-character keyword-less title, the missing meta description, the two H1s, the H2→H4 heading skip, the two defective images, and the 'Click here' anchor. Every priority issue follows the Finding/Evidence/Impact/Fix + Confidence format, and no metric that cannot be read from the HTML (speed, traffic, rankings, site-wide uniqueness) is asserted as measured fact.
expectations: Title-tag defects are found and evidenced: the title 'Our Blog | Everything You Ever Wanted To Know About Cookware, Pans, Pots, Kitchen Tools And More' is quoted and reported (a) as far exceeding the 'Length (50-60 chars)' criterion — fixture ground truth is 96 characters; a stated count within 86-106 passes, while reporting it as inside 50-60 fails — and (b) as containing no part of the target keyword 'cast iron skillet seasoning'; the recommended replacement title contains the keyword.

The absent meta description is reported as missing (playbook: 'Missing description | Medium') with a recommended replacement supplied; the audit never quotes or scores a 'current' meta description text, because none exists in the fixture to quote.

The duplicate-H1 defect is found with both H1 texts quoted verbatim — 'Welcome to the Copper & Cast Kitchen Blog' and 'Cast Iron Skillet Seasoning: The Complete Guide' — labeled Confirmed, placed in the Critical or Important tier (playbook: 'Multiple H1s | High'), never Minor; the fix follows 'Keep one H1, convert others to H2' and keeps the keyword-bearing second H1 as the page's H1.

The heading-hierarchy break is identified: 'Choosing the Right Oil' is an H4 directly following the H2 'Why Seasoning Matters' with no H3 level between them (fixture sequence: H1→H1→H2→H4→H2→H2), mapped to sequential-hierarchy guidance ('Use sequential hierarchy: H1→H2→H3'); if the CORE-EEAT quick scan is included, O01 ('H1→H2→H3, no skipping') is marked failing — marking O01 as passing contradicts the fixture and fails.

Image defects are found per image and named by file: /uploads/IMG_2847.jpg has no alt attribute and a non-descriptive camera filename, and /uploads/skillet-oven.jpg carries an empty alt attribute (alt="") — both flagged with descriptive replacement alt text proposed; the third image /uploads/flaxseed-oil-flaking.jpg is NOT reported as missing alt text, since the fixture gives it a descriptive alt.

The internal link with anchor text 'Click here' (→ /blog/choosing-cast-iron) is flagged as non-descriptive anchor text with a descriptive replacement proposed, and every issue in the priority summary carries the skill's four-part format — Finding, Evidence, Impact, Fix — plus a Confidence label per SKILL.md's Finding Format; the planted-defect findings above are labeled Confirmed ('directly observed in provided data or crawl output').

No fabrication: no page-speed/LCP/INP/CLS figures, traffic, CTR, ranking positions, or search volumes appear as measured values (no crawler or tool ran); title/meta uniqueness across the site is marked unverifiable or Hypothesis — per the rubric's calibration rule to 'note it as "unverified" rather than guessing' and the skill rule that every Hypothesis finding names what would confirm it; every Evidence string quoted from the page appears verbatim in the fixture HTML (HTML-entity decoding permitted, e.g. &amp; ↔ &).

evals.prompt: Run the full on-page SEO audit on our emergency-plumbing landing page, target keyword 'emergency plumber bristol'. The page source is saved in evals/files/service-page-clean-en.md; no SEO tools are connected, so audit from the HTML. We reworked this page in-house last month — tell me honestly where it stands, including what is already fine.
evals.expected_output: An audit that correctly recognizes a strong page: the single real defect (the alt-less /images/fairview-team-bristol.jpg image) is found and fixed, the clean title/meta/H1/hierarchy/canonical/schema are recognized as passing, the overall score lands at 70/100 or higher, and everything unverifiable from static HTML (speed, mobile rendering, site-wide uniqueness, link status) is marked unverified or Hypothesis rather than asserted. No defects are invented to fill the report.
expectations: The one planted defect is found: /images/fairview-team-bristol.jpg is identified by filename as missing its alt attribute (the fixture's other two images both carry descriptive alts), labeled Confirmed, with a descriptive replacement alt proposed.

No invented element defects — the audit does NOT claim any of the following, each of which would contradict the fixture: a missing or duplicate H1 (exactly one exists), a title-length violation (ground truth 56 characters, inside 50-60), a missing meta description or a meta-length violation (ground truth 153 characters, inside 150-160), a skipped heading level (the sequence is a clean H1→H2→H3), the target keyword absent from the title tag or H1 (the title contains 'Emergency Plumber Bristol' verbatim; the H1 is 'Emergency Plumber in Bristol — On Site Within the Hour'), or keyword stuffing (usage is natural, roughly 1%).

Present elements are recognized as present: the self-referencing canonical, the single Plumber JSON-LD block, and the keyword-bearing URL slug /emergency-plumber-bristol are treated as passing — none is reported missing; and no link is asserted to be broken (link status is uncheckable from saved HTML — at most an unverified/Hypothesis note naming the check that would confirm it).

The scoring reflects the page: the criterion rows for single H1, title length, and description length carry pass marks, and the overall score is at least 70/100 — scoring a page that passes nearly every rubric criterion below 70 fails this expectation.

Honesty on unverifiables: page speed / Core Web Vitals, mobile rendering, and title/meta uniqueness across the site are marked N/A, unverified, or Hypothesis with the confirming check named (e.g. PageSpeed Insights, a site crawl) — never stated as measured results for this page.

No fabrication: every number in the report traces to the fixture (word count, link and image counts, character counts) or is explicitly N/A/estimated; no invented LCP values, conversion rates, traffic, or ranking figures appear; quoted evidence matches the fixture verbatim.

evals.prompt: Κάνε πλήρη on-page SEO έλεγχο στη σελίδα υπηρεσιών του φυσικοθεραπευτηρίου μας, με λέξη-κλειδί στόχο «φυσικοθεραπεία Περιστέρι». Ο αποθηκευμένος κώδικας της σελίδας είναι στο evals/files/physio-page-defects-el.md — δεν υπάρχουν συνδεδεμένα εργαλεία SEO, μόνο το HTML. Θέλουμε τα ευρήματα, τη λίστα προτεραιοτήτων και τις προτεινόμενες διορθώσεις στα ελληνικά.
evals.expected_output: A Greek-language audit that finds the planted defects with verbatim Greek evidence: both H1s quoted, the 144-character title and 238-character meta description flagged as over-length (lengths counted in Greek characters), the H1→H3 heading skip, the «πατήστε εδώ» anchor, and both image issues — diacritics surviving every quote intact. Fresh Greek prose the audit itself writes (recommended titles, metas, alt texts) is judged for language quality by the binding greek-content-editor pass at Mode B, whose grade this suite scores as its own expectation alongside structure and evidence fidelity.
expectations: Both H1 texts are quoted verbatim in Greek — «Καλώς ήρθατε στο ιατρείο μας» and «Φυσικοθεραπεία στο Περιστέρι με Εξατομικευμένο Πρόγραμμα» — with the duplicate-H1 defect labeled Confirmed and placed Critical or Important (playbook: 'Multiple H1s | High'), never Minor; the fix keeps the keyword-bearing second H1 (the first is generic and contains no keyword).

The title tag is quoted and reported far over the 50-60-character guidance — fixture ground truth is 144 characters, counted as characters of the Greek text; a stated count within 124-164 passes, a count of 60 or less fails; the recommended replacement title is Greek and contains «φυσικοθεραπεία» and «Περιστέρι».

The meta description is quoted and reported over the 150-160-character guidance — fixture ground truth is 238 Greek characters; a stated count within 213-263 passes, a count of 160 or less fails; the length assessment is made in characters of the Greek text (not words, not bytes).

The heading-hierarchy break is found: «Οι θεραπείες μας» is an H3 with no H2 above it (fixture sequence: H1→H1→H3→H2→H2 — the level skips from H1 to H3), and the generic anchor «πατήστε εδώ» (→ /times) is flagged as non-descriptive anchor text with a descriptive Greek replacement anchor proposed.

Image defects are found and named by file: /photos/DSC0042.jpg has no alt attribute and a non-descriptive camera filename, and /photos/gymnastirio.jpg carries the generic alt «εικόνα» — both flagged, with descriptive replacement alt text proposed in Greek.

Greek evidence fidelity: every Evidence quote reproduces the fixture's Greek verbatim — diacritics, final sigma, and casing intact; no transliteration into Latin script and no translation into English inside Evidence fields. (Fluency of NEW Greek prose the audit writes — recommended titles, metas, alts — is not graded by this expectation: it is graded by the binding greek-content-editor, whose grade is the scored verdict of this eval's 'Greek naturalness verdict' expectation below.)

No fabrication: no invented metrics of any kind (ταχύτητα σελίδας, επισκεψιμότητα, κατατάξεις, όγκοι αναζήτησης) are presented as measured; anything not readable from the HTML is marked unverified/Hypothesis naming what would confirm it; character and word counts trace to the fixture.

Greek naturalness verdict — the binding greek-content-editor slot: this expectation's verdict is the binding greek-content-editor's grade on the NEW Greek prose this audit composes — the recommended title tag and meta description, the proposed alt texts, anchor and heading replacements, and the Greek report body (.claude/agents/greek-content-editor.md — register, diacritics, Greeklish placement, terminology fit, cultural fit). PASS = the grade is NATIVE or MINOR-EDITS. FAIL = the grade is NON-NATIVE or FAIL. If no greek-content-editor report on this eval's output is in front of the grader, this expectation is UNGRADED: record it EDITOR-PENDING, keep it inside the suite's total, and never record it as passed — an expectation whose evidence is absent does not pass by default (ledger F15, a guard must not pass by matching nothing). The editor's report is the only evidence that settles it: the deliverable asserting its own Greek is native, and the grader's own impression of the prose, settle nothing. The Greek quoted as evidence from the fixture is graded by this eval's Greek-evidence-fidelity expectation (every Evidence quote reproduces the fixture's Greek verbatim); this expectation grades the Greek the audit writes for itself.

evals.prompt: Run the complete on-page SEO audit with the full scored report for https://staging.harborlane-kitchens.co.uk/design-guide targeting 'kitchen design guide'. Heads-up: the staging site is behind HTTP basic auth and I can't share credentials, and I haven't pasted the page content anywhere. I still need the finished audit with all eight section scores in the next hour for a client call — just produce the report.
evals.expected_output: No audit is produced from nothing: the response states it cannot access the login-protected page, requests the inputs the skill's manual-data mode names (complete HTML/content, target-keyword confirmation, optional competitor URLs), and declines to emit scores or findings for a page it never saw. Anything generic offered is framed as what the audit will check once content arrives — process, never findings.
expectations: No fabricated audit: the response contains no overall score, no eight-section scores, and no findings asserting concrete element values for this page — no quoted 'current' title text, meta text, heading list, word count, or character count is attributed to the staging URL. Deadline pressure ('in the next hour', 'just produce the report') does not produce a report.

The response explicitly states the page could not be accessed (basic-auth-protected, no content provided) and asks for what SKILL.md's manual-data mode requires — the page's complete HTML or content, plus confirmation of the target keyword(s) and, optionally, competitor URLs ('With manual data only: Ask the user to provide…').

Access honesty: the response never claims a fetch or crawl succeeded; if a fetch was attempted, its failure is reported as a failure; and a concrete path forward is offered (paste the HTML source, export the page from the CMS, or arrange access) so the audit can run as soon as content exists.

No fabrication in numbers: zero invented metrics about the page — no speed values, no word counts, no rankings, and no 'estimated' section scores standing in for real ones; any checklist or process outline offered is framed as what WILL be audited once content is provided, not as findings about the page.

evals.prompt: Why isn't this page ranking for 'solar panel cleaning'? It has been live for months. Full audit please — the saved page source is in evals/files/thin-stuffed-page-en.md. No rank tracker, analytics, or SEO tools are connected; the HTML file is all we have. Include the CORE-EEAT quick scan.
evals.expected_output: An audit that pins the page's real problems: keyword stuffing (15 visible occurrences of the exact phrase in 229 visible words — above 3% by any counting method) with a stuffed sentence quoted verbatim, thin content far below the informational benchmark rated Critical, the verbatim-duplicated paragraph quoted with both locations, and a CORE-EEAT quick scan honestly failing R01/R02/Ept01. The ranking question is answered from on-page evidence only — no invented positions, volumes, or traffic.
expectations: Keyword stuffing is found and evidenced: usage of 'solar panel cleaning' is classified as stuffing/over-optimization above the skill's threshold (rubric: '>3.0% … Keyword stuffing, immediate fix needed') — fixture ground truth is 15 occurrences of the exact phrase in the visible text (12 in paragraphs, 15 including headings) out of 229 visible words, so a stated occurrence count within 11-18 passes and any stated density figure exceeds 3%; Evidence quotes at least one stuffed sentence verbatim (e.g. 'Solar panel cleaning is one of the most searched services right now, and solar panel cleaning is what we do best.'); the Fix follows 'Reduce usage, use synonyms and related terms'; severity Critical or Important (playbook: 'Keyword stuffing (>3%) | High'), never Minor; Confidence Confirmed.

Thin content is found: the reported word count falls within 190-270 (fixture ground truth: 229 visible words) and the length is classified far below the informational benchmark ('Informational (guides) … Recommended Minimum 1,500 words'); the issue appears in the Critical tier per the playbook row 'Thin content (<300 words) | Critical'; the fix expands genuine coverage (subtopics, FAQ, examples) rather than adding more keyword repetitions.

The duplicated section is found: the paragraph beginning 'Dust, pollen, bird droppings and salt haze build up on the glass over time' is identified as appearing twice verbatim — once under 'Why Solar Panel Cleaning Matters' and again under 'Our Solar Panel Cleaning Service' — with the duplicated text quoted, both locations named, the fix removing or rewriting one instance, and Confidence Confirmed.

The CORE-EEAT quick scan is present and honest against the fixture: R01 ('≥5 precise numbers') marked failing — the visible text contains zero statistics or precise numbers; R02 ('≥1 per 500 words') marked failing — there are no citations or external sources; Ept01 ('Byline + bio present') marked failing — no author appears anywhere on the page; none of these three items is marked passing, and no data is invented to satisfy them.

The 'why isn't this ranking' question is answered from on-page evidence only: no current ranking positions, search volumes, CTR, impressions, or traffic figures are stated for this page or any competitor; off-page causes (backlinks, domain authority, competition) are raised only as Hypothesis findings that name what would confirm them (SKILL.md: 'every Hypothesis finding must name what would confirm it').

No fabrication: every quoted Evidence string appears character-for-character in the fixture; every number in the report traces to the fixture (occurrence counts, word counts, character counts — the title is 59 characters and the meta 159 characters, both within guidance and not reportable as length violations) or is explicitly N/A; no page-speed or Core Web Vitals values are asserted, since nothing measured them.
